# Conf42

> Conf42 runs free online tech conferences (SRE, DevOps, DevSecOps, Cloud Native, Kubernetes, Platform Engineering, Observability, LLMs, AI agents, MLOps, Golang, Python, Rust, JavaScript and more). Every talk has its own page with the video, abstract, speaker bio and transcript.

## Blog
- [All posts](https://www.conf42.com/blog): talk previews, conference roundups, sponsor keynotes, webinars
- [Record, replay, fork: debugging an agent that failed mid-run](https://www.conf42.com/2026-11-09-record-replay-fork-failed-agent-runs): Reza Amini (Flashback) at Conf42 MLOps 2026 on saving agent runs as cassettes so you can rewind to the bad step and fork a fix instead of re-running.
- [Your LangGraph.js agent works. Can it survive a restart?](https://www.conf42.com/2026-11-09-operating-langgraph-js-agents-with-skein-js): Maina Wycliffe (Garatropic) at Conf42 MLOps 2026 introduces skein-js, a self-hosted runtime for LangGraph.js agents that pause, retry and restart.
- [Multi-agent systems need protocols before they need more agents](https://www.conf42.com/2026-11-09-multi-agent-systems-need-protocols-not-vibes): Daniel Akhabue (Qucoon) at Conf42 MLOps 2026 on typed messages, retries, dead-letter queues and tracing for agents that talk to agents.
- [LLMday Tel Aviv brings data engineering and AI agents to one room](https://www.conf42.com/2026-11-09-llmday-tel-aviv-data-meets-agents): LLMday Tel Aviv, November 17 at Microsoft Reactor - free talks from FalkorDB, groundcover, Komodor, Snyk and TeraSky on agents, graphs and data.
- [Fifty Claude agents in production: let the AI suggest, code decide](https://www.conf42.com/2026-11-09-fifty-agents-in-production-what-held-up): Muhammad Haris Farooq (Ruby AI) at Conf42 MLOps 2026 on running 50+ Bedrock agents: judges that see tool output, cache traps, and a 75% cost cut.
- [AI gardening: agent context drifts, so prune it on purpose](https://www.conf42.com/2026-11-09-ai-gardening-context-memory-entropy): Ishan Shah (PayPal) at Conf42 MLOps 2026 on AI Gardening: treating context and memory in long-running agent workflows as production state you maintain.
- [Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026: when agents become platform users](https://www.conf42.com/2026-11-06-platform-engineering-2026-roundup-agents-as-users): The Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 roundup - 26 talks on agents as platform users, delegated authority, GenAI as a platform primitive and real-time data.
- [What an engineering platform owes its AI agents](https://www.conf42.com/2026-11-05-harness-what-platforms-owe-coding-agents): Jimmy Caputo of Harness at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on the context layer, tools, guardrails and observability agents need to ship safely.
- [Terraform and Ansible are tools; the operating model is the architecture](https://www.conf42.com/2026-11-03-terraform-ansible-not-an-architecture): Jeleel Muibi of HybridOps at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on authority, preflight checks and run records that sit above Terraform and Ansible.
- [Power plant AI maintenance runs on context, not more sensor data](https://www.conf42.com/2026-11-02-ai-maintenance-power-plants-context-over-data): Mohan Kumar Dalai of GE Vernova at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on AI maintenance platforms that read context, cut alarm floods and keep humans in charge.
- [Replace the system the business runs on without a big-bang weekend](https://www.conf42.com/2026-11-01-zero-downtime-platform-migration-playbook): Saikrishna Ala (Bath and Body Works) at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on dual-write, bidirectional sync and CDC as reusable migration capability.
- [Gate every automated IT fix on a confidence score](https://www.conf42.com/2026-10-31-confidence-gated-agents-for-self-healing-ops): Madhu Chenna (Electronic Arts) at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 presents ADOF, a reference architecture for self-healing IT ops with confidence-gated AI agents.
- [Conf42 Prompt Engineering 2026 - the prompt is the smallest part](https://www.conf42.com/2026-10-30-prompt-engineering-2026-roundup-the-prompt-is-not-the-system): Conf42 Prompt Engineering 2026 in review, 18 talks on context contracts, prompt drift, injection defence, regulated workflows and agents in production.
- [Platform SLOs should stop the clock at ready, not provisioned](https://www.conf42.com/2026-10-30-platform-slos-that-stop-the-clock-at-ready): Amith Reddy Ravuru (Reltio) at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on journey SLOs that measure a developer's path from request to production-ready.
- [Your agent's evals passed. The canary is where it actually gets tested](https://www.conf42.com/2026-10-29-agent-evals-need-a-canary-in-production): Nicolas Zelaya of Harness at Conf42 Prompt Engineering 2026 on offline evals, versioned AI configs and agent canaries as one release loop.
- [Monitoring belongs in the deploy, not in someone's memory](https://www.conf42.com/2026-10-28-make-monitoring-a-deploy-step): Eleftheria Batsou (UptimeRobot) at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on creating monitors from the pipeline with a CLI, and what still needs a human.
- [Model-as-a-service on Kubernetes is database-as-a-service again](https://www.conf42.com/2026-10-27-model-as-a-service-is-database-as-a-service): Sergey Pronin (Solanica, OpenEverest) at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on serving LLMs with KServe, vLLM, an AI gateway and per-key token limits.
- [Put frontend standards in the platform, not in the prompt](https://www.conf42.com/2026-10-26-guardrails-for-ai-generated-frontends): Niharika P Pujari (McGraw Hill) at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on guardrails for AI-generated frontends with design systems, Storybook, Playwright, axe-core and CI.
- [PayPal moves the compliance gate onto the paved road with MCP](https://www.conf42.com/2026-10-25-paypal-puts-compliance-gate-on-paved-road): Sumeet L. Ram (PayPal) at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on exposing a geo-expansion platform to agents over MCP while people keep approving the rules.
- [MazeWall lets a JVM app sandbox its own threads with seccomp](https://www.conf42.com/2026-10-24-mazewall-lets-jvm-apps-sandbox-themselves): Leanid Piliptsevich (EPAM) at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 introduces MazeWall, using seccomp and Landlock to restrict pieces of an app from inside.
- [T-Mobile treats the T-Life app shell as an internal platform](https://www.conf42.com/2026-10-22-t-mobile-t-life-app-shell-as-platform): RanjithKumar Ragavan (T-Mobile) at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on how five teams ship into one 53-million-user mobile app without breaking each other.
- [With AI coding, the delivery bottleneck moves to code review](https://www.conf42.com/2026-10-21-ai-coding-moves-the-bottleneck-to-review): Lucas Mazei (Memed) at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 applies the theory of constraints to AI-assisted delivery and shows where platform teams should push.
- [A platform team of one runs side projects with AI, not on AI](https://www.conf42.com/2026-10-20-platform-team-of-one-ai-side-projects): Shem Magnezi (Lemonade) at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on running many AI-built side projects alone with minimal launches, recoverable paths and agents.
- [The smallest internal platform: a plugin-based Dev Mode for Android](https://www.conf42.com/2026-10-19-robofinance-dev-mode-plugin-framework-android): Denis Galkin (Robofinance) at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on turning scattered debug menus into a plugin-based Dev Mode framework inside the app.
- [Kafka won't make your retail supply chain resilient on its own](https://www.conf42.com/2026-10-18-kafka-wont-make-your-supply-chain-resilient): Nidhin Jose (Walmart) at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on the ownership, idempotency and recovery patterns that make event-driven retail systems hold up.
- [In real-time bidding, a late answer is a no answer](https://www.conf42.com/2026-10-16-in-real-time-bidding-late-means-no): Sujan Challa (Samsung Electronics America) at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on building an ad auction platform around a 100 ms latency wall.
- [Conf42 Feature Flags 2026: kill switches, migrations and model gates](https://www.conf42.com/2026-10-16-conf42-feature-flags-2026-roundup): Conf42 Feature Flags 2026 roundup: 16 talks from Harness, Capital One, Adobe, Bank of America, Confluent and more on flags for AI agents, migrations and models.
- [Feature flags turn a migration into a ramp you can walk back down](https://www.conf42.com/2026-10-15-feature-flags-make-migrations-reversible): Ryan Vila of Harness at Conf42 Feature Flags 2026 on gradual, measurable, reversible cloud-native migrations, and the flag hygiene that keeps them safe.
- [Debezium Platform turns CDC from a ticket queue into self-service](https://www.conf42.com/2026-10-15-debezium-platform-ends-cdc-ticket-queue): Vincenzo Santonastaso (IBM, Debezium maintainer) at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on scaling change data capture across teams with Debezium Platform.
- [BetBoom's own Dota 2 draft feed took conversion from 8.4% to 31.2%](https://www.conf42.com/2026-10-14-betboom-built-its-own-dota-2-draft-feed): Egor Kolovertnykh of BetBoom at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on turning Dota 2 Game State Integration snapshots into a live draft feed.
- [Treat tokens like money: a GenAI gateway with budget holds](https://www.conf42.com/2026-10-13-genai-platform-gateway-budget-holds-cache-failover): Brindal Patel of Coinbase at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on a GenAI gateway with card-style token budgets, safe semantic caching and eval-gated failover.
- [Pack five metrics into one LLM judge call, but not forty](https://www.conf42.com/2026-10-12-packing-llm-judge-metrics-cost-accuracy): Scarlett Attensil of LaunchDarkly at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on how many criteria one LLM judge can score before accuracy slips.
- [The feature store behind every For You feed, explained](https://www.conf42.com/2026-10-10-feature-store-infra-behind-for-you-pages): Attila Toth of ScyllaDB at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on online feature stores, P99 tail latency, query-first data models and pluggable stores.
- [A correct diagnosis doesn't give an AI agent the authority to act](https://www.conf42.com/2026-10-09-ai-agents-need-delegated-authority-not-permissions): Ruby Agarwal, VP of Engineering at Avaya, at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on scoped, expiring authority for agents that remediate production.
- [A Claw is a coding agent that never logs off](https://www.conf42.com/2026-10-08-personal-coding-agent-claws-explained): Erik Hanchett of AWS at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on Claws, the always-on coding agents with memory, schedules, chat apps and sandboxes.
- [Agent engineering starts by assuming the model gets fooled](https://www.conf42.com/2026-10-07-agent-engineering-assume-the-model-gets-fooled): Cynthia Akiotu of Accenture at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on identity, MCP tools and authorization checks that hold when prompt injection works.
- [Your agent orchestrator won't save your money; the thin controller will](https://www.conf42.com/2026-10-06-agent-orchestrator-thin-controller-saves-money): Yedidya Schwartz, CTO of Quicklizard, at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on crashing six durable engines to see who pays twice for model calls.
- [Conf42 DevSecOps 2026 roundup: checking agents before they act](https://www.conf42.com/2026-10-02-devsecops-2026-roundup-agents-at-the-gate): Conf42 DevSecOps 2026 in review, from hooks that gate coding agents and SBOMs that stop at the model to cell isolation, masking checks and safe recovery.
- [Your coding agent's dotfiles are the new software supply chain](https://www.conf42.com/2026-10-01-agent-dotfiles-new-supply-chain-harness): Roshan Piyush of Harness at Conf42 DevSecOps 2026 on why hooks, skills, memory and MCP servers are where AI supply chain attacks now land.
- [Conf42 AI Agents 2026: less LLM, more harness](https://www.conf42.com/2026-09-25-conf42-ai-agents-2026-roundup): Conf42 AI Agents 2026 roundup - planning without model calls, AI coding harnesses, LLM-as-judge testing, runaway token bills and agent security, in 22 talks.
- [Enterprise AI in four pillars: context, evals, memory, governance](https://www.conf42.com/2026-09-24-enterprise-ai-four-pillars-harness): Shubham Jindal of Harness at Conf42 AI Agents 2026 on why AI demos stall before production, and the four pillars that get agents there.

- [Green dashboards only show the paths you have already tested](https://www.conf42.com/2026-09-10-green-dashboards-cant-prove-resilience): Uma Mukkara of Harness at Conf42 Observability 2026 on why green dashboards can't prove resilience, and a four-step loop to test the untested paths.

- [Resilience Testing Is Non-Negotiable in the Enterprise SDLC](https://www.conf42.com/2026-03-19-harness): Outages in distributed systems are inevitable, making resilience testing essential in the SDLC. It must be continuous, covering failures, load, and disasters. Delayed validation creates “resilience debt,” increasing risk. A holistic approach—combining chaos, load, and DR testing—plus cross-team collaboration and AI-driven insights improves reliability and reduces impact.
